title: Long Short-Term Memory — 1997 Neural Computation Publication Milestone
summary: On 15 November 1997, Sepp Hochreiter and Jürgen Schmidhuber published "Long Short-Term Memory" in Neural Computation. The paper presents the long short-term memory approach for recurrent learning and addresses the problem of decaying error backflow over extended time intervals.
significance: A directly identifiable publication milestone for long short-term memory (LSTM) in recurrent neural-network research. LINEAiGE records the dated publication event without treating it as an unsupported universal invention date, first implementation date, or proof of later causal influence.

verification.note: MIT Press gives the article title, authors, Neural Computation volume 9 issue 8, pages 1735-1780, DOI, and publication date 15 November 1997. PubMed independently reports the same date, journal, volume, issue, pages, authors, and DOI. This candidate is restricted to the publication milestone and does not infer an earlier development date, universal priority, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship edges.

candidateMeta.admissionReason: The publisher record and independent bibliographic corroboration support a stable, day-precision 1997 publication milestone for the LSTM paper while keeping publication chronology separate from system-origin and causal claims.
candidateMeta.nextStep: Before canonical admission, reconcile this publication milestone with Hochreiter's earlier work on long-term dependency problems and any primary-source evidence for pre-publication LSTM development, preserving separate milestones unless the evidence supports consolidation.
